budget_note: Per-BOARD, not per-group. test-board carries 8 kicad: groups (one per Zener module), which the naive 'groups exist -> 20 per group' reading would turn into 160 iterations. They fail the decomposability test in Step 9.2: the modules all fight over the same 21mm of width, their nets are mostly NOT internal, and none can succeed or fail on its own -- U1 sits in the middle of every one of them.

findings: min_clearance_used 0.127 -- below HW-TB-PCB07's 0.15 HARD floor. --track-width-floor bounds WIDTH; nothing bounds clearance. The standard 2-layer fab tier floor IS 0.127.
XOUT leg routed 3/3 in its own pass and arrived BROKEN in the final board: the bulk pass ripped it. Step 2c exclusion stops re-routing, not ripping.

iterations.parent_board_note: The chain writes every placement to the same path, so this filename ALSO named iteration 1's rejected 20-lock board. Caught by the routing-feedback verifier lens. Iteration 2 established the 24-lock set and iteration 3 extended it to 26 (R7/R8); the chain's place_optimize call carries all 26, so every board from iteration 3 on descends from the ACCEPTED placement. Reusing an output path across iterations makes a ledger unauditable -- a real process defect, recorded rather than papered over.

stop_condition.fired: 2 - budget/effort exhausted, reported with the remaining blockers itemised
stop_condition.detail: Ten iterations of a 20-per-board budget. Stopped short of the budget on wall-clock, not because the levers were exhausted: the two remaining large components have identified but unaffordable levers (broken=10 needs --rip-blocker-nets, which does not finish here -- FINDINGS B10) or no lever at all (the QSPI <=15mm rule cannot be expressed to the router -- FINDINGS B9). The board is NOT finished and is not presented as finished.
hard_clauses_unmet: HW-TB-PCB13 0.8mm USB (72.3%/77.6% on the connector segments; impossible on the MCU side, bisected)
HW-TB-PCB14 2.4mm 3W (152 violations; 121 in the unsatisfiable fan-out annulus, 21 in open channel)
HW-TB-PCB19 QSPI <=15mm (CS chain 21.49mm; SCLK/SD0/SD1 unrouted; no --max-length exists)
HW-TB-PCB24 GND pour continuity under USB/QSPI (violated; graded by NOTHING in the chain)
HW-TB-PCB25 VCC3V3/VBUS >=0.4mm (48 of 132 VCC3V3 segments under)
HW-TB-PCB26 three fiducials (board has zero; never in the netlist)

score.note: graded at the board's own classes. The 23 figure quoted earlier was a re-grade at --clearance 0.15, which is LOOSER than the 0.16 Default class and hides 16 real violations. Neither number is right for a multi-class board -- check_drc grades one scalar (FINDINGS B7).

corrections_after_verification.why: check_spec.py built its path graph from segment ENDPOINTS only, so every T-junction read as a break. Directly tested afterwards: strip all 52 copper locks, run the bulk pass with --max-ripup 20 and the XTAL nets excluded -> XTAL segments 32 before, 32 after. Exclusion IS sufficient; the skill was right. lock_nets.py stays as belt-and-braces but is not load-bearing.
